title: Fix: Coldest Reading
summary: A method meant to return the lowest temperature reading returns 0 on warm days. Find out why and fix it.
statement:
`coldest(temps)` should return the lowest value in `temps`, a non-empty array of whole-degree readings.

The code below was written for a winter dashboard and seemed fine there. On a warm day it reports a temperature that was never measured.

Reproduce the problem with the public cases, work out which line causes it, and fix it. Any correct fix is accepted: it doesn't have to match a reference.

examples.explanation: Every reading is above 0; the lowest is still one of them.

hints: Run the public cases. Which one fails, and what do the readings in the passing cases have that the failing one doesn't?
Look at the value `coldest` holds before the loop sees any reading. Can a reading ever beat it if every reading is above it?
Start from a value that really is one of the readings, such as temps[0], or from the largest int, so the first reading always replaces it.

lab.intended_behavior: Return the lowest reading in a non-empty array, whatever the season.

defect.summary: The running minimum starts at 0, a value that isn't one of the readings.
defect.explanation: `coldest` begins at 0, and a reading only replaces it when it's lower. When every reading is above 0, none of them is lower, so the method returns the 0 it started with: a temperature nobody measured.
defect.why_missed: The code was tried on winter data. With at least one reading below 0, that reading replaces the starting 0 straight away, so the bad starting value never shows.

lab.follow_up: Whenever code keeps a running best (a minimum, a maximum, a first match), check what it starts from and try a case where no input beats that start.
